name: What Are the Most Common ADU Construction Mistakes?

mainEntity.name: What are the most common mistakes homeowners make when building an ADU in Los Angeles County?
mainEntity.text: What are the most common mistakes homeowners make when building an ADU in Los Angeles County?

acceptedAnswer.text: The biggest ADU mistakes usually happen before construction even starts. Homeowners often choose a design they like without confirming whether the site can actually support it, which leads to redesigns after plan review. Another common issue is underestimating utility upgrades, especially electrical panel capacity, sewer connections, water service, and trenching. People also frequently forget about drainage, fire access, storage, privacy, and how the ADU will fit with the existing driveway or yard. Budget mistakes are equally common, especially when homeowners do not include contingency for permit revisions or hidden site conditions. In Los Angeles County, an experienced contractor should help you evaluate the parcel first, then guide the design toward a buildable, code-conscious layout. The safest approach is to complete a feasibility review, confirm the utility path, set a realistic contingency, and decide on finishes only after the structure and plan are confirmed. That sequence reduces change orders and schedule surprises.
acceptedAnswer.description: The most common mistakes are skipping feasibility checks, underestimating utility upgrades, choosing a design before verifying setbacks, and approving a budget without contingency. Many homeowners also overlook drainage, access, storage, and long lead times for materials and inspections.
